snippet.title: Dungeons & Dragons - Warriors Of The Eternal Sun (1992, SEGA MD / GENESIS Gameplay 2020)
snippet.description:
Dungeons & Dragons - Warriors Of The Eternal Sun is an Isometric RPG that uses D&D rules. The game was released in 1992, it was developed by Westwood Associates, and published by SEGA.


NOTE: I'm NOT a fan of these type of isometric view Dungeon & Dragon games, so.. I will try and keep this review as non-biased as I can, though unexpectedly this one wasn't that bad to get used to the controls.


STORY: 10/20
Amidst the eve of a battle your castle and entire town is teleported to a strange land that is surrounded by mountains and has a burning red sun in the sky. Your team of warriors are tasked with exploring the surrounding areas and recruiting new allies or your town will perish.

GRAPHICS: 8/20
The graphics are seen from an isometric top-down viewpoint, almost like a God simulation game but without the auto features. The game is not as great graphically as other RPG games for the system but early D&D games are not very well known for their great graphics. The colors of the graphics for the town, castle, areas, etc are all nice and vibrant colored, even your characters are clothes brightly which is nice, it enables you to actually see what class they are supposed to be.

SOUND: 8/20
The sound is okay but you can tell it's years old. Each areas seems to have it's own music track, the world travel has it's own track and even when entering into combat with the enemy. Sound effects are all okay too, be it entering into menu system, using items, spell casting, attacking, etc.. there's not many sound effects but it's effective in what it is trying to achieve.

GAMEPLAY: 12/20
The gameplay start with you either choosing a pre-made team by the game itself OR you can create your own team using the systems D&D rules. In game you roam around like any other normal game exploring areas and defeating monsters, all whilst looking for allies for your town. When battling the enemy you have weapons and magic at your disposal, depending on what slot you put them in is dependent on what button you press to use it.,. so usually 'A' is your weapon and 'B' is magic spell you have assigned your character to use. 

There's an option to run from battle but to be honest it's not worth it, you fail way too often, your only option really is to be sure you SAVE often enough so you don't lose much progression if you die. The game is open world so you can end up exploring places you shouldn't really be at which will result in you dying horribly, this is why the SAVE feature comes in handy. 

SYSTEMS: 10/20
There's a couple of different systems in this game but not that many over all. The save system is really useful, the fact you can save whenever as long as you are not in battle, this can help loads but gets a bit tedious after a short while saving every few minutes. There is an artifact system in place where if you find any items you can take back to an NPC in the town's castle and he will appraise the item for you, he will then give you Gold for the item, thus allowing you to buy better equipment for your team. There are shops in this game where you can buy weapons, items, magics, and even armor for your party, this will help them survive better out in the world. Once equipping Magics you can learn them permanently by resting your party so they will have access to the spell indefinitely if you are lucky.

OVER ALL: 48/100
Unexpectedly, I quite enjoyed this game but it certainly didn't have enough for me to want to carry on playing it to the very end, I can see it becoming quite the chore looking for monsters to slay just to level, I like my RPGs to level much faster and with less missing attacks in battle. The music was okay but nothing special so i'd probably end up putting my own music on to listen to eventually. The constant missing of attacks were really starting to annoy me, it almost felt like the game want's you to fail whenever possible. Would I recommend this game today? if you're an early D&D game fan then yes, I would recommend it but if not then i'd say move on.
 
------------------------------------------------------------------

Have you played this game? What did you think? Let me know in the comments below.

Don't forget to Like, Comment, and Subscribe to my Channel guys!!

Thanks!
